column3: The Hebrew repeats the blessing root in a noun and verb; BSB has “the blessing” and “pronounced.”
The Hebrew says He dawned “to them”; BSB has “upon us.” The Hebrew says He came “from” holy myriads, while BSB says “with myriads of holy ones.”
The Hebrew has plural “peoples” and says “His holy ones”; BSB has singular “the people” and “the holy ones.”
The Hebrew says Moses “commanded” the law; BSB says he “gave” it.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name who became king here; BSB supplies “the LORD.”
The Hebrew’s final clause has no explicit negative word; BSB introduces it with “nor.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins both Thummim and Urim to “Your godly man” without an explicit giving verb; BSB supplies “Give” and assigns the Thummim explicitly “to Levi.”
The Hebrew says “I have not seen him” in the singular and then uses plural verbs for keeping the word and covenant; BSB has “them” and then singular “he.”
The Hebrew uses plural verbs for teaching and setting incense, places incense in God’s nose, and has singular “whole offering”; BSB uses “He,” “before You,” and plural “whole burnt offerings.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “between his shoulders” without explicitly naming God in the shielding clause; BSB says “upon His shoulders” and supplies “God.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “moons” or months; BSB says “the seasons.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “the bush” without an explicit word “burning”; BSB supplies “burning.”
The Hebrew directly calls his horns “horns of a wild ox”; BSB marks the comparison with “like.”
The Hebrew has singular “your going out”; BSB uses plural “your journeys.”
The Hebrew says they will “suck” the abundance of the seas and repeats the sacrificing root in verb and noun; BSB has “feast on” and “offer sacrifices.”
The Hebrew joins the arm and head with “also”; BSB uses “or.” BSB also supplies “the domain of” before Gad.
The Hebrew ends with “with Israel”; BSB says “for Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew addresses Naphtali directly with a singular command to inherit; BSB says “he shall take possession.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name a gate; BSB supplies “of your gate.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives the command “Destroy” without an explicit object; BSB supplies “him.”
The Hebrew says “alone” and “his heavens”; BSB has “untroubled” and “the heavens.”
Close to the Hebrew.
